capabilities: Render a refraction lens behind each floating glass surface (toolbar, menus, command palette, notices, status bar)
Add chromatic dispersion, rim light and a pointer-following highlight to glass
Adjust glass tint, strength and performance via settings, including a battery saver
Add header cards with icon and description to settings pages
Move window controls into the settings sidebar on macOS
disambiguation: Not a standalone theme or visual effect; it only works on top of the Tahoe theme, which provides the glass surfaces.
extras: Desktop only and made on macOS. Runs pmset -g once a minute to detect low power mode (read-only) and uses Electron's window API for the settings window controls; the README states there is no network use, telemetry, ads, accounts or payments. Not affiliated with or endorsed by Apple.
intentEvidence: Real refraction for the Tahoe theme's glass.
motivation: The author notes that CSS can blur what's behind a surface but can't bend it, so the plugin draws a lens for each floating surface instead.
problem: CSS backdrop blur can only blur what is behind a surface, so Obsidian themes cannot make floating UI actually bend the content behind it like real glass.

relations.evidence: It needs the Tahoe theme: with another theme there's no glass for it to bend.
With Tahoe Run: the ▶ Run capsules on code blocks get the same glass.
The bend across the rim follows Liquid Glass Studio by Charles Yin (MIT)

summary: Companion to the Tahoe theme that renders real refraction, dispersion, glare and a pointer highlight on its glass surfaces, plus header cards on settings pages.
